segments.text: In this tutorial we learn asynchronous programming in Python with asyncio.
Async lets a single thread handle many I O bound tasks concurrently.
You define a coroutine using the async def keyword.
Inside a coroutine you use await to pause until a result is ready.
The event loop schedules coroutines and resumes them when awaited work finishes.
Use asyncio dot run to start the event loop from synchronous code.
To run tasks concurrently wrap them with asyncio dot gather.
Gather returns results in the same order as the input coroutines.
A common mistake is calling a blocking function inside a coroutine.
Blocking calls freeze the event loop and stall every other task.
Offload blocking work with asyncio dot to thread to keep the loop responsive.
Always set a timeout on network calls to avoid hanging forever.
Use asyncio dot wait for to enforce a timeout on any awaitable.
Cancellation propagates by raising CancelledError inside the coroutine.
That wraps up the basics of async and await in Python.
